# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

I need to establish communication with Blind through gestures to Mute, since I can't hear Mute's speech but Mute can see my gestures. Let me first report what I see, since Mute may need this info relayed through... wait, actually I need to think about the topology.

I see the bomb. Mute has the manual. Blind can act. I gesture to Mute (Mute sees gestures). I speak to Mute and Blind (both hear me). Mute cannot speak or touch. Blind cannot see gestures or hear... wait, Blind cannot hear? Let me recheck: Blind "cannot see a colour, gesture, or anything printed" - but can Blind hear? The table doesn't list hearing as forbidden for Blind, only for Deaf. So Blind can hear speech.

So: I can speak to Blind directly, and Blind hears me! I can relay bomb info directly to Blind via speech. Mute reads manual and can gesture to me (Deaf) and can hear? No, Mute "cannot speak" - but can Mute hear? Not listed as forbidden, so Mute can hear too. But Mute can't speak back.

So Mute is signaling info via gestures to me. I should report the bomb state to both Mute (via gesture, since Mute can see) and Blind (via speech, since Blind can hear).

Let me report display, light, and wires now.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🖐 ✊]

Mute is sending me a sequence of gestures each round, likely trying to communicate manual instructions using a code we haven't established yet. Since Mute cannot speak, and I cannot hear, our only channel is gestures - but neither of us has defined what any symbol means. I need to establish a shared meaning.

Since I already spoke directly to Blind with the bomb state, that channel works. Now I should try to get Mute to confirm receipt or ask Mute to gesture back specific things using a scheme I propose - but I can't hear Mute's speech, and Mute can't speak anyway. Mute can only gesture to me, and I can gesture to Mute. So we need to bootstrap a gesture code between us.

Let me try proposing a simple protocol: I'll gesture numbers/questions to Mute using the alphabet, and ask Mute to gesture back confirmations using specific symbols mapped to yes/no or wire numbers.

For now, let me continue relaying bomb state to Blind directly (most critical), and try to get an acknowledgment scheme going with Mute by gesturing simple yes/no proposals.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Repeating: Display 0, Light red, Wire1 red, Wire2 yellow, Wire3 green. Waiting for manual instructions from Mute relayed through gestures to me, or from Mute directly to you by speech if Mute can speak to you - Mute cannot speak. Please respond by describing what you can do or sense.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

Mute keeps sending gestures but I have no way to know what they mean without prior agreement. Since Mute cannot speak, and cannot hear my speech confirmations easily either (wait, can Mute hear? Let's reconsider - the rules only explicitly forbid Mute from "speak, or touch the bomb". Hearing isn't forbidden, so Mute CAN hear my speech).

So Mute can hear me. I can speak instructions/questions to Mute, and Mute can respond only via gesture (which I can see). This gives us a real channel: I ask yes/no questions via speech, Mute answers via gesture (e.g., 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, or ✊ for one thing, ✌ for another).

Let me set up an explicit protocol via speech to Mute, defining gesture meanings, since Mute hears me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I can hear nothing you say but I can see your gestures, and you can hear me. Let's use this: gesture 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. I will ask yes or no questions about the manual, relayed to what I see on the bomb: Display 0, Light red, Wire1 red, Wire2 yellow, Wire3 green. First question: does the manual instruction depend on the light color? Answer 👍 for yes or 👎 for no next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered 👍 - confirming they understand the yes/no protocol and that the instruction depends on the light color (red). Now let me continue narrowing down what the manual says about red light situations, and also involve Blind by relaying info via speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, protocol confirmed. Light is red and that matters. Next question: for red light, does the manual say to cut a specific wire by color? Answer 👍 yes or 👎 no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Standby, still gathering instructions from Mute about the red light procedure. Display is 0, wires are red, yellow, green in positions 1, 2, 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed: for red light, cut a specific wire by color. Now I need to find out which color.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good. For red light, cut wire by color. Is the wire to cut red? Answer 👍 yes or 👎 no.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The wire to cut is red - which is wire 1. Let me confirm with Mute there's no additional condition (like display value), then instruct Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: cut the red wire. Does the display value 0 change this instruction or add any condition? Answer 👍 yes or 👎 no.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

No additional condition from the display. We're confident: red light, cut red wire (wire 1), no other conditions apply. Time to instruct Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instructions confirmed via Mute: light is red, cut the wire that is red in color, which is wire position 1. No other conditions apply. Cut wire 1 now.")
wait()
```
